title: Shared Database Integration (Database-as-IPC)
pattern: Direct database sharing where multiple independent microservices or modules read/write directly to the same database schema instead of communicating through public API boundaries.
why_bad: It tightly couples the services' physical representations [38:442]. If Service B refactors its database tables, Service A silently breaks at compile time or runtime. It bypasses Domain Domain boundaries, violates encapsulation, and prevents independent service deployment [21:123].
detection: Querying tables that conceptually belong to a different microservice bounded context or module, or sharing database connection pools across domain module boundaries [442:442].
fix: Enforce schema ownership per service. Keep database schemas strictly private to each service, forcing all inter-service communication to pass through explicit published APIs (gRPC, HTTP DTOs, or event messages) [38:442].
source: *Fundamentals of Software Architecture* (Richards & Ford) [21:123]; *Implementing Domain-Driven Design* (Vernon), Chapter 13 [442:442].
